metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [September 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.50

context:
## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [September 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.50
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.50
- Datum: 09.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah and Manfred, as Lotte is lazy and writes only short
letters it is to the Hausbuch[?] to write all what happened. We
like the city and the people enormously and we are delighted
how much sympathy in all the important quaters exists for
England, how much pity for France; the newspapers are in contrast
with the Northamericans absolutely partial for England and express
openly the hope that Hitlers attacks will fail. English ships come
from time to time but one does better to write by air over
Newyork, it takes sometimes only 10 days. My plans are not
quite definite, I have a lecture, well paid, in San Pablo and
here I will there for speak for some charitable purpose, then
Uruguay 2 lectures and Buenos Aires and Chile; our expenses will
largely be covered and I have time to write meanwhile. I ad-
mire Rio every day more, it is the most colourful, the most
fascinating town I know, full of surprises and new beauties; it
develops with a rapidity what seems unbelievable - we went
to day in the tram just an hour (for two American cents) and
have not seen half of the city. Today we had two receptions
Lotte had not less then four ministers for conversation (and
with the former ambanador Cortin five) first at the reception
for the Uruguay minister, where she sat at the side of the foreign
minister then in a party given in her honour (or ours) at the
minister of communications - one charming house and with lots of
gardens with views one only can dream. Yesterday we had long
nightly auto drives along the ocean and over the mountains, to
morrow we have the minister of Cuba for tea and meanwhile she
fits and talks, - often too much because I want to explore
this town and there are so many parts we have not yet inspected.
I would like to live now there except here would it not be for
the heat which hinders my work as I was able to see in Newyork
- but they are already constructing air conditioned houses here
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig. Der Text am linken Rand ist eine vertikale Fortsetzung des Textes, die hier in den Haupttext integriert wurde, da sie den Satzfluss ergänzt. Die Tinte ist violett. Die Lesbarkeit ist gut.
Rückseite des Dokuments mit Archiv-Farbskala und Grauskala.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar. Einige Wörter wie 'Hausbuch' sind aufgrund der Handschrift leicht unsicher, aber im Kontext plausibel.
